diocese: The Episcopal Church of New Hampshire
sourceFile: Diocesan events calendar, fetched directly from https://www.nhepiscopal.org/events (individual weekly "Diocesan Cycle of Prayer" calendar events).
notes: This is a Squarespace events-calendar page, not a standalone cycle-of-prayer document; it lists individual weekly events titled "Diocesan Cycle of Prayer - <subject>" alongside unrelated event types (e.g. "Bishop's Visitation ...", "General Convention ...") that were excluded here as not part of the cycle of prayer itself. Only events whose title begins "Diocesan Cycle of Prayer" are transcribed.

The page shows a rolling window (an "upcoming" list plus a "past events" list below a divider), not a single full-year document. When fetched 2026-09-29, the Diocesan Cycle of Prayer events present ran 2026-05-31 through 2027-01-17 with no gaps (one per Sunday). Only the 2026-dated entries (2026-05-31 through 2026-12-27, 31 weeks) are included in this file per this corpus's one-file-per-diocese-per-year convention; three further entries dated 2027-01-03, 2027-01-10, and 2027-01-17 were present on the same page but belong to a future year's file, not this one. Entries for January-April 2026 were not present on the page at fetch time (they had aged out of the rolling window) and are not fabricated here.

Each week's event title is printed as "<subject> / <intention>" (or, on one week, 2026-12-27, with no slash at all). The clause before the slash generally names a specific congregation or diocesan entity; the clause after the slash is a themed prayer intention (e.g. "for an end to gun violence") that does not always name a discrete group. Since this schema's subject types are limited to 'parish' and 'category' for a diocese-level file, each intention clause is recorded here as its own 'category' subject with the source's own printed text as its `name`, kept verbatim including the leading word "for" -- this is a judgment call to fit the source's two-clause week titles into the schema's subject list rather than an attempt to rename or paraphrase them into conventional category names like "Diocesan Staff".

The left-hand clause was treated as a 'parish' subject (name + place) only when it named what reads as one specific congregation; entries naming a camp/conference center, a diocesan school, a network/ministry, or "the churches in" a town collectively were instead recorded as 'category' subjects with the full printed text (including the place, where given) kept in `name` since subjectShape's `place` field applies only to type 'parish'.

"Christ Church and Holy Trinity Lutheran, Portsmouth" (2026-08-09) is transcribed as a single parish subject exactly as printed; it is not clear from the source whether this names one shared Episcopal-Lutheran congregation or two separate congregations sharing a location/listing, so it was not split into two subjects.

The source itself is inconsistent in how it abbreviates "Saint": "St. James Church, Sunapee" (2026-09-06) vs. "Saint James Church, Laconia" (2026-12-13) -- both preserved exactly as printed, not normalized to a single style.
No week in this source carries a liturgical Sunday label (e.g. "Proper 20"); `liturgicalNote` is null throughout because the source printed none, not because it was omitted.
Each event's own description field was checked and found empty for every entry transcribed here -- all subject/intention content came from the event title alone.
